raw_text:
We need to answer whether each choice occurs after time 1200. Let's analyze.

At 1200, tasks running with remaining times listed. After 1200, no new submissions, no machine failures (M08 doesn't return). We must simulate until tasks finish, and machine returns? None. So tasks will finish; some may start as resources free. The tasks in queue waiting start when capacity becomes available. We need to determine case for each choice:

0: task T049 will start on machine M01  
Currently T049 is in waiting list with submitted time 798, priority 0, CPU 3125, memory 777, run time 167. It can start on any machine with enough free CPU/memory. Let's check machine capacities for resources we need: CPU 3125, memory 777. Which machines have that capacity? Machines listed: M01: CPU 6250 memory 3116; M02: 6250 6244; M03: 3125 3123; M04: 6250 6244; M05: 6250 3116; M06: 6250 3116; M07: 6250 6244; M08: down? M08 is down but doesn't return in this window (never). So available machines up at time 1200: all up except M08 down. Are any running tasks on machines? Yes list indicates running tasks. We need check free CPU and memory on each at time 1200.

But scheduling policy uses reservation and backfilling. We need to know if T049 will start on M01. Let's analyze step by step.

At time 1200, before scheduling round occurs? Actually at 1200 we have events: finishes, failures, returns, submissions, then scheduling round. At time 1200 there are finishes: T074, T075, T076 finish, freeing resources on M01, M03, M06. Others may finish also? T100 start M03 at 1200, so no finish. So after finishes, we have tasks currently running after finishes, as listed. The running list shows remaining times assuming they were started earlier.

Now at scheduling round at time 1200, the waiting tasks list will be considered. The order is queue order with priority. Need to compute; but easier maybe to quick simulate: tasks with priority 9 first: list has T003 (priority 9), T101, T102. Also maybe others? T003 is priority 9. They will be scheduled accordingly. But we just care about T049 (priority 0). It's later.

Potential reserved machine: may be assigned earlier tasks to reduce waiting time. But to see if T049 will start on M01, we need to see whether some earlier tasks will occupy M01 at times when available. Let's evaluate resource timings.

Let's list tasks on each machine with remaining times (start time, remaining at 1200, thus finish time):

M01: T038 started 888 remaining 120 -> finish at 1008. T039 remaining 29 -> finish at 1200? It started 888, remaining 29 => finish at 917? Wait start 888 + remaining 120? hold on: start times: Looking at running list indicates started times: T038 started 888, remaining 120, so finish at 1008. T039 started 888 remaining 29 finish 917. T080 started 1075 remaining 265 finish 1340. T017 started 756 remaining 255 finish 1011? start 756 + remaining 255 = 1011. T077 started 1025 remaining 9 finish 1034. T079 started 1195 remaining 493 finish 1688. T082 started 1200 remaining 390 finish 1590. Wait T082 started at 1200, so it's starting now. T009 started 341 remaining 226 finish 567.

M03: T013 started 605 remaining 406 finish 1011. T081 started 1075 remaining 257 finish 1332. T100 started 1200 remaining 246 finish 1446.

M04: T078 started 1110 remaining 3775 finish 4885.

M05: T017 running same as earlier? Actually T017 M05? Wait table: T017 on M05 earlier. Already counted. So no other.

M06: T077 on M06? It started 1025 remain 9 finish 1034. T079 on M06 started 1195 remain 493 finish 1688. T082 on M06 started 1200 remain 390 finish 1590. T009 on M07. Good.

M07: T009 on M07 finish 567.

M05 and M06 both have tasks etc.

Now after 1200 starts scheduling round. The waiting tasks include T049. We should determine whether T049 can start on some machine. At time 1200, the first machine to get a slot maybe M07? But T009 will finish at 567, already finished. So free at 1200. Actually T009 finished earlier; after 1200 it's not running. So free CPU/memory equal full capacity. For M07 capacity 6250/6244. T049 needs 3125/777; fits. So likely T049 could start on M07 if earlier tasks are scheduled there. But we need to consider ordering and reservations. Let's examine the first tasks to schedule: T003, T101, T102 (priority 9). Their CPU/memory: T003 CPU 6250 free 10340 memory, so needs huge; can start maybe on M04 or some big machine? M04 capacity 6250/6244; memory is 6244; but T003 needs 10340 memory > 6244, so cannot fit. Since no machine has that memory, T003 will never start and will stay waiting forever. That will block subsequent tasks? In scheduling rule, a task that cannot fit on any up machine even if empty gets no reservation and keeps waiting; the next task that cannot start may then get the reservation. But that means T003 occupies first priority slot but cannot start, so no reservations issued? Wait step: In scheduling round, tasks are taken one at a time. For each task:
- Try first fit
- If none and no reservation yet and production task, try preemption (eviction) etc.
- If cannot start by a or b, the first such task gets a reservation. Also latter tasks may start by first fit but on reserved machine only if fits within reservation.

So with T003 not fitting, it gets a reservation because it's the first task that cannot start. That means it will reserve earliest time it could start, computed from tasks currently running, on first machine in id order where that time is reached. Let's determine earliest start time for T003. It needs CPU 6250 memory 10340. No machine has enough memory. So it will never start. According to policy: "A task that would not fit on any up machine even if that machine were empty gets no reservation and simply keeps waiting; the next task that cannot start may then get the reservation." So T003 gets no reservation, stays waiting. Then scheduler proceeds to next task T101. Since T003 cannot start and no reservation yet, T101 will attempt first fit. T101 CPU 6250 memory 10340 as well if priority 9 (J36). So also cannot start. It will also get no reservation. Then T102 (priority 9) same code: cannot start. After those three, no reservation assigned yet. Next tasks priority 4: T071? It is priority 4. Let's evaluate if it can fit. T071 CPU 6250 memory 1553. Memory needed 1553; capacity of machines: M04, M01 etc have memory 3116, 6244, etc, all >1553. So fits. So T071 will attempt first fit. Which machine first in id order has enough free resources? We need current state before scheduling round: all running tasks still running; so machine availability includes free CPU and memory left on each. Let's compute used CPU/memory for each machine at 1200.

We need to sum CPU and memory used by tasks running on each machine, then subtract from capacity to determine free.

We'll need CPU and memory per task from running list.

Let's list per task details: From running list we have for each task: CPU, memory, running.

T038 CPU 1874, memory 777 on M01. T039 1250, 1166 on M01. T080 1250, 610 on M01. T017 1874, 777 on M05? Wait CPU 1874, memory 777, that's T017, machine M05. T077 1250,466 on M06. T079 3125,466 on M06. T082 1250,610 on M06. T009 6250,4773 on M07.

Also T013 6250,4773 on M02. T081 1250,610 on M03. T100 1874,777 on M03.

T078 6250,3528 on M04.

That's it.

Let's compute capacity per machine:

M01 capacity CPU 6250 mem 3116.
Occupied: T038 (1874,777), T039 (1250,1166), T080 (1250,610). Total CPU used 1874+1250+1250=4374. Remaining CPU 1876. Memory used 777+1166+610=2553. Remaining memory 3116-2553=563.

M02 CPU 6250 mem 6244. Occupied: T013 (6250,4773). CPU used 6250: remaining 0. Memory used 4773, remaining 1471.

M03 CPU 3125 mem 3123. Occupied: T081 (1250,610) + T100 (1874,777) = CPU used 3124, remaining 1. Memory used 610+777=1387, remaining 1736. (Note also T013 on M02 not relevant.)

M04 CPU 6250 mem 6244. Occupied: T078 (6250,3528). CPU 6250: remaining 0. Memory used 3528, remaining 2716.

M05 CPU 6250 mem 3116. Occupied: T017 (1874,777). CPU used 1874, remain 4376. Memory used 777, remain 2339.

M06 CPU 6250 mem 3116. Occupied: T077 (1250,466)+T079 (3125,466)+T082 (1250,610)= CPU 1250+3125+1250=5625, remain 625. Memory used 466+466+610=1542, remain 1574.

M07 CPU 6250 mem 6244. Occupied: T009 (6250,4773). CPU used 6250 remain 0. Memory used 4773, remain 1471.

M08 down; ignore.

Now, first fit: T071 priority 4, CPU 6250 memory 1553. Find first machine id order with free CPU >=6250 and memory >=1553. Let's check:

M01 free CPU 1876 <6250: no.

M02 free CPU 0 <6250: no.

M03 free CPU 1 <6250: no.

M04 free CPU 0 <6250: no.

M05 free CPU 4376 <6250: no.

M06 free CPU 625 >=6250? No.

Thus none have CPU >=6250 since we have tasks using nearly full capacity on some machines; but which machines have free CPU enough? None.

Therefore T071 cannot start by first fit. Next, preemption? T071 is production task (priority 4? Wait priorities 9-11 production, 0-1 free tier, 2-3 maybe interim? Actually definition: priorities 9-11 production tier; priorities 0 and 1 free tier. So priority 4 is not production. Preemption applies only for production tasks. So T071 cannot preempt. Thus T071 cannot start, no reservation as no reservation yet? Wait a reservation is granted to first task that cannot start from a or b if no reservation yet. So T071 will get a reservation. This is the first reservation. The reservation will be computed as earliest time it could start on some machine with free resources after considering current running tasks. Let's compute earliest start time.

We need to consider time when a machine will have enough CPU and memory free for T071.

We need to analyze each machine free capacity over time. But maybe easier: Which machine could ever have enough free CPU? Only those machines with capacity 6250 cpu and memory maybe 3116-6244. For T071 needs 6250 CPU. That means only machines with 6250 capacity can host it (all except M03). But which machines have 6250 capacity and have enough free memory: M01 memory remaining 563 <1553, not enough. M04 remaining memory 2716 >1553 but CPU 0. So will need to wait until some task finishes and frees enough CPU. Similarly M05 memory 2339 >1553, CPU 4376 <6250. M06 memory 1574 >1553 but CPU 625 <6250. M02 memory 1471 <1553, but CPU 0. M07 memory 1471 <1553, CPU 0.

Thus only machines that can satisfy memory after some finish are M01, M04, M05, M06 maybe. but all have memory enough except M02, M07. Among them, the earliest time when CPU frees to >=6250.

Machine M01 will get CPU freed when tasks finish on it. Currently free CPU 1876; tasks running are: T038 with remaining 120, T039 remaining 29, T080 remaining 265. These tasks finish at times 1200+120=1320, 1200+29=1229? Wait T039 remaining 29 finishes at 1229. T038 finishes at 1320. T080 finishes at 1465. So at 1229, T039 finishes; CPU freed 1250, so free CPU becomes 1876+1250=3126 still <6250. At 1320, T038 finishes, free 1874 => free CPU 3126+1874=5000 still <6250. At 1465, T080 finishes, free 1250 => free CPU 6250. So earliest time machine M01 can host T071 is 1465. Similarly check memory: at that time free memory cumulative accordingly but memory needed 1553; before 1465, memory free as of after each finish? Currently free memory 563. After T039 finish (memory 1166), free memory becomes 563+1166=1729 >=1553. So memory will be enough when T039 finishes at 1229, but CPU not enough until 1465. So earliest start 1465 on M01.

Check M04: currently free CPU 0, memory 2716. Task running T078 on M04 will finish at time 1110+3775=4885, so never. So M04 will never free CPU. So no.

M05: free CPU 4376 <6250, memory 2339 >1553. Will free CPU when tasks finish on M05. Only T017: remaining 255 => finish at 1200+255=1455. After that, free CPU 4376+1874=6250. So earliest start time 1455 on M05.

M06: free CPU 625<6250; memory 1574>1553. Only tasks finish: T082 finishes at 1590; T077 finishes at 1034 (past), T079 at 1688. So until 1590 free CPU 625+1250=1875? Actually at 1590, T082 finishes freeing 1250, making free CPU 625+1250=1875 <6250. So CPU never fully freed. So M06 cannot host.

Thus earliest overall start time for T071 is 1455 (M05). So reservation for T071 will be on M05 at time 1455.

Now later tasks may start on the reserved machine M05 as long as they finish before reservation time or fit into free after.

But for tasks with lower priority like T049 priority 0, they might start earlier on other machines where resources free earlier (e.g., M07 free at 1200). But preemption may happen? Only production tasks preempt. So T049 cannot preempt. So T049 will attempt first fit among free machines at scheduling round after earlier tasks. But earlier tasks could occupy machines before T049's turn, reducing free resources. Need to simulate order of scheduling round at 1200. Tasks in queue order: After T071, the waiting list order continues: T096,97,98,99,010,041-048,049,051,053-068,069,072,073,083-095.

Priorities: T096-99 priority 4. T010 priority 0. T041-048 priority 0. T049 priority 0. etc.

But because earlier tasks may be scheduled concurrently in same round, we need to see when the scheduler picks each. In round:

- First task: T003 cannot start => hold/wait
- T101 cannot start => hold
- T102 cannot start => hold
- T071 reservation on M05 start time 1455.
- Next tasks T096(4) will try first fit. After previous tasks, machine states: After T071 reservation assigned but no resource allocation yet (reservation doesn't occupy resources). So machine free state same as before: M07 free etc. T096 CPU 6250 mem 3107. Which machine has both CPU 6250 and memory >=3107? Let's check capacities: M01 memory 3116 >3107 but CPU 6250 and machine M01 has free CPU 1876 so can't. M02 memory 6244 >3107 but CPU 6250 but free CPU 0. M03 memory 3123 >3107, free CPU 1. M04 memory 6244 >3107, free CPU 0. M05 memory 3116 >3107, free CPU 4376. M06 memory 3116 >3107, free CPU 625. M07 memory 6244 >3107, free CPU 0. So none free. Wait M02 memory 6244 but free CPU 0; can't. So T096 cannot start by first fit. It's a production task? priority 4 not production. So cannot preempt. So it will get a reservation? It will be the first task that cannot start by a or b since T071 already has reservation. Wait reservation only if no reservation yet; if already one exists, tasks may still get reservation? The algorithm: first task that cannot start by a or b gets a reservation, but reservation is only for the first such task when no reservation for that round? The policy: "The first task in the round that can start neither by a. nor by b. gets a reservation" So if there is already a reservation, later tasks will not get reservation again. However earlier tasks after T071 that cannot start might also not get reservation because reservation already set. They will simply keep waiting until maybe later rounds? Actually they might start later when resources free but they can't because no reservation and no preemption. So they persist waiting. So after T071, no further reservations can for round. So T096 cannot start. So moves to next round.

Thus tasks of lower priority will keep waiting until later when resources free and scheduling round again after events change. After tasks finish, scheduling rounds happen at times of events: finishes, failures, returns, etc. So when any task completes, a new scheduling round is triggered, and the waiting list is processed again.

Thus we need to simulate timeline of finishes and attempt to start waiting tasks when resources free. We need to know when T049 will possibly start, and if on M01.

Let's simulate until T049 starts.

We know T049 is priority 0 with CPU 3125, memory 777. It needs machine with at least those capacities. Which machines have such? We'll evaluate each machine's timeline to find earliest time it can start T049 given machine usage.

Check each machine:

M01: current tasks finish times: T039 1229, T038 1320, T080 1465. After 1229, free CPU becomes 3126 and memory 1729. After 1320, free CPU 5000 memory 2506. After 1465, free CPU 6250 memory? final memory 2506+610? Wait T080 memory 610; after 1465 free memory 2506+610=3116. So at 1465, full capacity. That's earliest time for T049 on M01 maybe; but earlier than 1465? At 1229, free CPU 3126 <3125? Wait need 3125 CPU, 5924? Wait requirement 3125 CPU, 777 memory. At 1229, free CPU 3126 >=3125, memory 1729 >=777. Thus T049 could start at 1229 on M01. However, is there any reservation that might block it? The reservation for T071 is on M05 at 1455. That does not affect M01. So T049 could start at 1229 if scheduling round at 1229 attempts it.

But is there a scheduling round at 1229? Finishes occur at 1229 (T039), 1320, 1465 etc. After each finish, a round occurs. At 1229, after T039 finishes, tasks remaining: T038, T080, others. At that time, the waiting list still starts with T071? Actually after failures/finis, new round processes waiting list again but the order is same waiting queue. So at 1229, the scheduler will try to schedule tasks, possibly T071 reservation will still be in effect? The reservation was set at time 1200, but results are not bound until that time; maybe the reservation remains for the round but might not persist across rounds? Let's understand: reservation computed in a round and applied to that round at start; it remains for the moment? The policy: "The first task in the round that can start neither by a. nor by b. gets a reservation: the earliest time at which it could start..." This is per scheduling round. After round, tasks that started occupy resources. Reservations not carried to next round? I think reservation is just a label for a partition of that round; after round ends, it doesn't persist. However, tasks that cannot start will remain waiting. In future rounds, they can again start. So reservations are not gating across rounds.

Thus T049 could start on M01 at 1229 if it can first fit after T039 finishes.

But we must consider that once scheduling round processes waiting list, the first task that can start (T071 was first but cannot, but still in waiting). After reservation, later tasks such as T096 may still not start. But when a round finishes, no tasks started yet (only reservation). That round might not allocate any tasks yet? Wait if no tasks could start, the round ends with no new starts. Then the waiting list remains unchanged. Next event occurs at next finish time.

But T049 requires 3125 CPU. That fits on M01 now. So at 1229, T049 may start if it's first waiting task that can fit; but the scheduler will try tasks in waiting order. But we need to verify no earlier tasks that can fit before T049 that may occupy M01. Let's evaluate earlier waiting tasks: after T071, we have T096 (CPU 6250). Can't start. T097,098,099 same. Now in round at 1320: start scheduling. The first tasks that can start with current free resources maybe again T043? T043 needs 3125 CPU; M01 free 1875 <3125; M02 0; M03 1; M04 0; M05 free CPU 1251 after T042? Wait T042 finished at 1346; but at 1320, T042 still running because started 1229+? Actually T042 start 1229 run time 117 => finish 1346. So at 1320 running. So M05 free CPU is still 1251? Wait no T042 running on M05 until 1346. So free CPU 1251. Not enough for 3125. T049 needs 3125 CPU. So not start yet. Next higher priority: T096 (production) CPU 6250 memory 3107 cannot start (needs 6250 CPU). No machine has free 6250 CPU. But maybe some machine will have 6250 free when tasks finish? But at this moment, not.

Start times:
T043 at 1340 (finish 1436)
T044 at 1436 (finish 1436+104=1540? Wait run time 104? T044 run time 104? Wait T044 run time 104? Actually run time 104 given in list: T044 J20 0 3125 777 104. Yes 104. So finish 1540.

Thus choice 0: true.

Next choice 1: T038 will finish no later than time 1320. We saw T038 finishes at 1320 (exact). So yes, T038 will finish no later than 1320. Good.

Choice 2: T078 will finish no later than time 5020. T078 had run time 3765 start 1110 finish 1110+3765=4875. Wait predicted earlier: start 1110 finish 4875. Compute: 3765 +1110 = 4875. 4875 < 5020. So yes finish before 5020. So true.
